threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 67 bus runs on a timetable. Everyone knows it’s just a suggestion.
Heard a guy on the 87 last night explaining the secret menu at his favourite chicken shop. Only opens after 1am—he swore it’s a game changer.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the guy at the corner bakery knew my order before I said it, and the sound of late-night shisha smoke wafted through my window.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you hear techno beats blasting from the outdoor markets during the day, blending street food with party vibes like a Berlin signature.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can name the exact taco cart that only pops up after 9 PM and still swear it's the best in the city.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 47 at Civic Center yesterday, and a guy was serenading everyone with a ukulele—strangely uplifting considering the delays.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the hipster cafés, but the real charm's in the quiet, winding streets where locals still chat over a game of dominoes.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still stare at the metro map like it’s a treasure map, convinced there’s a hidden route to get to Gràcia.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think saying "thank you" to bus drivers is normal. Around here, you just nod and look straight ahead.
Last night on the 35, a bloke was reciting Shakespeare like he was auditioning for the National. The whole bus was captivated, strange vibe in the air.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in flip-flops argue passionately with a busker over the best döner in town. Only in Neukölln do such debates get heated.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that serves beer brewed on-site. It's like a hidden culinary rebel against the norm.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows to walk through Dolores Park even when it smells like a mix of patchouli and dog pee. It’s just part of the vibe.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 5 here last week and we had to wait while a dog had its own little parade on the tracks—classic San Francisco chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the plaça just outside the metro is where all the real action is. But the true vibe hides behind the side streets, away from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You'll catch them hesitating at the pedestrian crossings, still unsure if the lights actually mean anything. It's a telltale sign.
